chapters.title: What this meeting studies
chapters.narrative: What the meeting studies (cancer types, domains, geography), then who drives it: sponsors say who runs the study, originators say who owns the drug — often not the same party.

chapters.title: How mature the evidence is
chapters.narrative: Staging, evidence type, overall assessment and study design together: which conclusions travel, and which are early signals only.

chapters.title: Which targets and mechanisms compete
chapters.narrative: Assets by drug, target and mechanism, plus the cancer type → target → drug pathways behind them.

chapters.title: How to read it and what to watch
chapters.narrative: Converging the previous acts into an actionable reading: layered conclusions, assets worth tracking, and gaps where evidence is still thin.

views.title: Most disclosed cancer types
views.requirement: Abstracts mentioning the cancer type; one abstract can count for several types, so shares sum to more than 100%.

views.title: Disease domains
views.requirement: By platform disease-domain tags; one abstract can belong to several domains.

views.title: Leading sponsors
views.requirement: Counted per sponsor; multi-sponsor studies count once per sponsor, investigator-initiated and registrational studies alike.

views.title: Leading drug originators
views.requirement: Counted per drug originator/holder — a different lens from sponsors above: the sponsor may be a hospital or CRO while the drug belongs to someone else. The field records the **current holder** of the drug, so backbone chemotherapies (carboplatin, paclitaxel, gemcitabine, oxaliplatin) are held by generic manufacturers and inflate their rank; read this together with the drug ranking when judging the innovative portfolio.

views.title: Originators most studied by external sponsors
views.requirement: Only studies whose sponsors do not include the drug originator: mostly academic, hospital or partner-led validation rather than originator-run registrational work. The same current-holder caveat applies, so generic holders of backbone chemotherapies cluster near the top.

views.title: Where the sponsors are based
views.requirement: By the country or region where the sponsor is registered.

views.title: Stage and setting
views.requirement: Platform stage tags, mixing trial phase (I/II/III) with disease setting (early, locally advanced, advanced). Abstracts without the tag are excluded.

views.title: Evidence types
views.requirement: By platform evidence-source tags: prospective or retrospective studies, real-world studies and trial phases each count separately.

views.title: Overall assessment
views.requirement: By platform result-assessment tags; unlabelled abstracts are shown as not assessed rather than counted as positive or unfavorable.

views.title: Stage by assessment
views.requirement: Abstracts per cross combination; empty cells are drawn as blank and mean no such study at this meeting.

views.title: Most studied targets
views.requirement: Abstracts mentioning the target; each target in a combination counts separately.

views.title: Most disclosed drugs
views.requirement: Abstracts per drug; a multi-arm abstract counts once per drug, and each drug in a combination counts separately.

views.title: Mechanisms of action
views.requirement: By platform mechanism-of-action tags; a drug may carry several.

views.title: Cancer type → target → drug
views.requirement: Only the most disclosed cancer types with their targets and drugs, to read the pathways rather than the full distribution.
